entities.name: Anthropic
entities.role: Frontier lab behind the Claude model family. $65B Series H at $965B; the most valuable AI company. Its IPO prospectus was obtained and reported by Reuters on 2026-09-28 but has still not appeared on EDGAR, so there is no public share count, price range or ticker and nothing to mark against - the reported document shows 2025 revenue up twelvefold to nearly $4.6B against a net loss of about $42B, roughly $34B of which is a non-cash remeasurement of convertible financing instruments rather than operations, an operating loss of $8.06B, $7.33B of compute and infrastructure spend, and nearly a quarter of revenue coming from just two customers on contracts that do not bind them to keep spending. It also sets out at least $518B of cloud, chip and infrastructure commitments over roughly ten years across six partners - about $111.1B to Google, $110B to Amazon, up to $84.5B to SpaceX and $31.4B to Microsoft - of which about 80% is non-cancelable or payable regardless of use - and a seventh leg, a six-year $35B deal with Lambda signed in late August 2026 for roughly 350 MW in Texas, has its own Bloomberg sourcing independent of the prospectus - and it warns investors of existential risks to humanity from advanced AI. Bankers have discussed an offering valuing the company above $2T. On 2026-09-24 it signed an $11.6B seven-year cloud agreement with Akamai for CPU capacity, taking a warrant for up to 5% of Akamai in the process. Amodei committed in September 2026 to give third-party evaluators permanent employee-level access to Anthropic's systems, a pledge OpenAI said it would match, and on 2026-09-12 published 'We Must Pace the Frontier', arguing the industry should slow capability gains - Altman and Musk both said they agreed; Trump publicly rejected the call two days later The FTC is reported to be expanding a sweeping product-safety probe of Anthropic, OpenAI and other frontier labs, with formal demands for information planned (2026-09-30). The reported prospectus also puts a five-year, $125.2B commitment for TPU computing capacity with BROADCOM as lessor, about a third of which Broadcom has agreed to finance itself through up to $42B of convertible notes (2026-10-01) - circular financing of the kind the map now sees repeatedly, and a structure the filing says carries potential conflicts of interest. Broadcom's syndicate began amassing $60B to fund that capacity on 2026-10-02 (Bloomberg) - a $42B senior-secured tranche being placed by Bank of America, Citigroup and Morgan Stanley alongside an $18B subordinated tranche led by Blackstone - which is the financing partner the prospectus allowed for rather than new money on top. Separately, Anthropic is reported to have begun ending the roughly 15% discounts it gives customers once they hit their usage limits, forcing mid-contract renegotiations (2026-10-01). As of 2026-10-05 the S-1 is STILL not on EDGAR, seven days after Reuters obtained and reported the document, so there is no public share count, price range or ticker and nothing to mark against. The SpaceX leg of those commitments is the one the map can read from a public filing rather than from the unfiled prospectus: SpaceX's own S-1 discloses the 2026-05-03 cloud services agreement at $1.25B a month through May 2029, and Anthropic has confirmed that figure. Microsoft is simultaneously a compute counterparty and a paying model customer: The Information reported on 2026-10-12 that Microsoft is on track to pay Anthropic more than $2B a year for the Claude models in Microsoft 365 Copilot, a single-source figure neither company has confirmed, while Microsoft and Meta are separately reported to have cut their own internal Claude spending. An EIGHTH compute counterparty surfaced on 2026-10-14: The Information reports an unannounced multiyear cloud agreement with IREN, with the value and length undisclosed and neither company confirming, which is why that edge is reported - and its framing is that the build-out increasingly depends on former bitcoin miners (IREN, Hut 8, TeraWulf, Nscale) because they control scarce grid connections. The shape of that Broadcom-arranged $60B is now reported in full and settles how it sits against the lease: the FT says the package, codenamed PROJECT NORTH STAR and financing roughly 1.5 GW of TPUs, is a $42B Class A senior-secured tranche plus an $18B Class B junior tranche led by Blackstone, of which Blackstone would hold $9B on its own book at a reported 10% coupon - with fees and issue discount taking its total return above that - and the other $9B would be syndicated to a wider group over the coming months, possibly at a lower yield. The junior debt is reported to be secured on the lease payments themselves, so the $18B is INSIDE the $60B that funds about a third of the $125.2B commitment rather than new money on top of it. The package has not closed. Separately, the company was reported to be meeting prospective IPO investors at its San Francisco headquarters on 2026-10-14 while its S-1 is still not public on EDGAR.

Anthropic's reported IPO prospectus (2026-10-01) discloses that Broadcom has agreed to lend Anthropic up to $42B via convertible notes - sized at roughly a third of a five-year, $125.2B commitment for TPU computing capacity on which Broadcom is the lessor, convertible into Anthropic equity, with Broadcom retaining the option to bring in a financing partner. THE TERMS ARE NOW IN BROADCOM'S OWN FILED 10-Q, which is a stronger footing than the unfiled Anthropic prospectus they were first reported from: the quarterly report for the period ended 2026-08-02 says that in connection with lease agreements that enable access to compute capacity, "our customer may, under certain circumstances and if needed, issue to us convertible promissory notes up to an aggregate principal amount of $42 billion", restricted to the customer's lease obligations, and that no notes had been issued as of 2026-08-02.
